godavari.label: Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Scheme — Godavari system
godavari.summary: The world's largest multi-stage lift scheme: Godavari water is pumped roughly 500 m uphill in a chain of barrages, tunnels and pump houses to reach the Deccan plateau.

totals.note: Government/press materials widely cite '618 m' as the total lift figure, but 618 m is Kondapochamma Sagar's absolute elevation above sea level — the cumulative lift from the Godavari at Medigadda works out closer to ~520-526 m.

krishna.label: Krishna system — predominantly gravity-fed
krishna.summary: From Jurala through Srisailam to Nagarjuna Sagar, Krishna water descends by gravity alone — no pumping on the main stem. Four large lift schemes branch off the Srisailam/Jurala foreshore to reach higher plateau land nearby.

liftSchemes.name: Kalwakurthy Lift Irrigation Scheme
liftSchemes.notes: 3 pumping stages, 4 balancing reservoirs; reported lift (298 m) doesn't exactly reconcile with the elevation gap (257.6 m) between the cited source and destination points.

liftSchemes.name: Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme
liftSchemes.notes: 5-stage pumping system designed to lift 90 TMC of monsoon floodwater over ~60 days; Phase I (Narlapur/Anjanagiri intake) inaugurated 2023.

liftSchemes.name: Dindi Lift Irrigation Scheme
liftSchemes.notes: Lifts up to 30 TMC across a 12-reservoir network; destination elevation not confirmed in available sources.

liftSchemes.name: Rajiv Bheema Lift Irrigation Scheme
liftSchemes.notes: Irrigates roughly 203,000 acres across Makthal, Atmakur, Wanaparthy and Kollapur.

dataNotes: Kaleshwaram's total lift is reported inconsistently: 618 m (Kondapochamma Sagar's elevation) vs ~520-526 m (computed cumulative lift from Medigadda). Both figures are shown; treat 618 m as elevation, not lift.
Kaleshwaram's official target capacity is 240 TMC (195 from Medigadda + 20 from SRSP diversion + 25 groundwater recharge) — a figure disputed by CAG audit and opposition sources.
Ananthagiri Reservoir's elevation (470 m) is interpolated between Mid Manair Dam and Ranganayaka Sagar — not independently confirmed.
Individual barrage capacities (e.g. Annaram: 10.87 vs 11.9 TMC) show minor inconsistencies across Wikipedia and news sources.

The Kalwakurthy scheme's reported total lift (298 m) does not arithmetically match its cited source/destination elevations (a 257.6 m gap) — likely reflects staging not captured by simple subtraction.

Map connector lines between reservoirs come in two kinds: solid lines follow a documented intake, canal or lift scheme (e.g. Kaleshwaram's offline chain, NSP left canal to Wyra/Palair, Srisailam/Jurala lift-scheme foreshores). Dashed lines (Kinnerasani, Laknavaram, Ramappa) connect a standalone tank to its nearest mapped hub purely for visual continuity and are not a claim about the actual engineered route.
